title: Purity conventions and the rank-one datum
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $n\geq1$, with the coefficient notation of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Put $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$. The prime $\ell$ is invertible on every scheme considered. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and the twists $K(m)=K\otimes^L_A A_T(m)$ [sk-def-sp-tate-twist, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Use the global base field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] in the finite-type scheme setting of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi). Whenever exceptional inverse images occur, schemes and morphisms are in that setting; $Rf^!$ is its constructible exceptional inverse image for every separated finite-type morphism $f$, without an ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility hypothesis.

For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], put $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. The zero section $s:Y\hookrightarrow X$ is given on $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$ by $R[t]\to R$, $t\mapsto0$. Its complementary open is $j:U=\mathbf G_{m,Y}\hookrightarrow X$, with affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,t^{-1}]$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. The same symbol $t$ denotes the coordinate on $X$ and its restriction, a unit on $U$.

For any $N\geq1$ with $\ell^N A=0$, the finite-level twist is canonically
$$
A_T(1)=\mu_{\ell^N,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A
\cong\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}A
$$
on the pro-etale site, with roots of unity and tensor products as in [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. These identifications use the power transitions on roots and are independent of $N$ [sk-def-sp-tate-twist, lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. One may always take $N=n$, since $(\ell^n)\subseteq(\varpi^n)$ in $\mathcal O_E$. If $e=e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)$ divides $n$, one may instead take $N=n/e$; then $(\varpi^n)=(\ell^N)$, and $A\cong\mathcal O_E/\ell^N\mathcal O_E\cong(\mathbf Z/\ell^N)^{ef}$ as a module, where $f=[\mathcal O_E/(\varpi):\mathbf F_\ell]$ [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level]. The condition $e\mid n$ is imposed only in this last freeness assertion.

Here is the precise meaning of the Kummer class with $A$ coefficients. On $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, use the exact sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]
$$
0\longrightarrow\mu_{\ell^N,U}^{\mathrm{et}}\longrightarrow\mathbf G_{m,U}
\xrightarrow{z\mapsto z^{\ell^N}}\mathbf G_{m,U}\longrightarrow0.
$$
Let $\delta_N(t)\in H^1(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mu_{\ell^N,U}^{\mathrm{et}})$ be its boundary, cohomology and connecting maps being those of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor]. Write $A_U^{\mathrm{et}}(1)=\mu_{\ell^N,U}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$ [def-pur-kummer-module-coefficients] and $\varphi_N(\zeta)=\zeta\otimes1_A$. Define
$$
\kappa(t):=\operatorname{comp}_U\bigl(H^1(\varphi_N)(\delta_N(t))\bigr)
\in H^1(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A_U(1)),
$$
where $\operatorname{comp}_U$ is the canonical etale/pro-etale cohomology comparison [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison]. The coefficient identification here is the following specified map, using the comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and its identification of finite constant coefficients [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. The natural root-sheaf map $\nu_U^{-1}\mu_{\ell^N,U}^{\mathrm{et}}\to\mu_{\ell^N,U}$ sends a root over an etale neighbourhood $V$, represented together with $W\to V$ in the inverse-image colimit, to its restriction on $W$. Clause (1) of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] gives an etale cover on which the pro-etale root sheaf is the constant module $\mathbf Z/\ell^N$. Restricting that trivialization to etale objects gives the same constant-module trivialization of the etale root sheaf: the root sections are the same unit solutions, while the finite constant sections agree by the finite-constant-sheaf identification above and degree-zero cohomology comparison on each etale object [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison]. The finite-constant-sheaf identification in [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] therefore makes the displayed map an isomorphism on this cover: in these trivializations it sends a residue class to itself. The local inverses glue, giving $\nu_U^{-1}\mu_{\ell^N,U}^{\mathrm{et}}\cong\mu_{\ell^N,U}$, compatibly with the power maps since restriction commutes with powers. Since this inverse image is a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint, applying it to the universal bilinear map defining the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] identifies $\nu_U^{-1}A_U^{\mathrm{et}}(1)$ with $A_U(1)$; the insertion map is sent to $\zeta\mapsto\zeta\otimes1_A$. Equivalently, $\delta_N(t)$ is the class of the root torsor
$$
\mathcal T_t=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_U\bigl(\mathcal O_U[T_0]/(T_0^{\ell^N}-t)\bigr),
$$
and $\kappa(t)$ is its class after extending the structure group by $\varphi_N$ and applying comparison [lem-sc-torsor-h1, lem-sc-etale-torsor-h1-functoriality, def-sc-contracted-product-presentation]. Thus coefficient extension is applied to the root sheaf and its class. The definition uses no module structure on $\mathbf G_m$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell^N$. The Kummer maps, the insertion $\zeta\mapsto\zeta\otimes1_A$, and comparison are natural for pullback; in particular the class is compatible with base change, and the power transitions identify the classes for different admissible $N$.

For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_Z$, use the normal cone [pur9-def-normal-cone]
$$
N_{Z/X}=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Z\Bigl(\bigoplus_{r\geq0}\mathcal I_Z^r/\mathcal I_Z^{r+1}\Bigr).
$$
Its zero section is induced by projection onto degree zero. Here regular of pure codimension $c\in\mathbb N$ means that each point of $Z$ has an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in $X$ on which the ideal is generated by an $R$-regular sequence of length $c$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], allowing the empty sequence for $c=0$. For such an immersion the conormal sheaf $\mathcal I_Z/\mathcal I_Z^2$ on $Z$ is locally free of rank $c$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and the canonical graded algebra map
$$
\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_Z}(\mathcal I_Z/\mathcal I_Z^2)\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{r\geq0}\mathcal I_Z^r/\mathcal I_Z^{r+1}
$$
is an isomorphism [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra, lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial]. Thus the cone is the rank-$c$ normal bundle, meaning the relative spectrum of this symmetric algebra, locally $\mathbf A^c_Z$ with linear changes of coordinates, with its augmentation zero section $z$.

For a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], separated finite-type $g:V\to B$ of finite-type $k$-schemes with a closed section $s:B\hookrightarrow V$ ($g\circ s=\operatorname{id}_B$), put $\omega_g=Rg^!A_B$. The section invariant is the actual pullback [def-pur-section-invariant]
$$
\mathcal C(g,s):=Ls^*\omega_g=Ls^*Rg^!A_B.
$$
The deformation to the normal cone of the section and its family object are those of [def-pur-dnc-section-family]:
$$
\mathcal D_sV:=\operatorname{Bl}_{s(B)\times\{0\}}(V\times_B\mathbf A^1_B)
\setminus\widetilde{V\times_B\{0\}},
\qquad
\mathcal F:=L\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g}
\in\operatorname{Pic}\bigl(D^b_{ctf}(\mathbf A^1_B,A)\bigr).
$$
Here the removed subscheme is the strict transform of the closed fibre, $\widetilde g:\mathcal D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_B$ is the structural morphism, and $\widetilde s:\mathbf A^1_B\to\mathcal D_sV$ is its induced section. The cone and deformation are these constructions attached to the given immersion or section, not arbitrary schemes supplied as data.

Finite twist: ell is a unit times varpi^e, so ell^n lies in (varpi^n) and N=n is always admissible; freeness of rank ef is claimed only when e divides n, which is exactly the hypothesis of lem-pur-finite-kummer-level. Kummer class: the sequence is exact because ell is invertible (lem-amb-kummer-any-base); the coefficient insertion uses def-pur-kummer-module-coefficients; the cohomology comparison is 099W, valid for any abelian etale sheaf. I confirmed the source error: G_m is not a Z/ell^N-module, so the source's tensored Kummer sequence is ill-typed. The item's reading (boundary first, then insertion) is the typed form of the source's own torsor description. Etale/pro-etale identification of the root and twist sheaves: the inline argument is correct. It uses the etale trivializing cover of lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free (1), the finite constant-ring comparison and the adjunction, and it follows the same pattern as the reviewed node def-pur-affine-line-datum. I found no existing node that states this identification, so no citation is missing. Torsor (03AJ): the map of short exact sequences [r]->r, a->t^a commutes, so delta_N(t) is exactly the class of the root torsor, with no sign; the level transitions are compatible. Normal cone: the regular-immersion condition matches Stacks definition-regular-ideal-sheaf and 063J; the rank-c bundle follows from 00LN via lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial and lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra; c=0 gives Z. Section invariant: the added separated finite-type domain is where sk-def-sf-operations(vi) defines Rg^!, and it agrees with def-pur-section-invariant. Deformation: the item follows def-pur-dnc-section-family verbatim; for g=s=id it gives A^1_B. Edge cases n=1 with e=2, an empty base, c=0 and the identity pair all check out. No SGA source is used, this is not a target node, and no tool_uses were needed. One item for maintenance: the unit record still names sec-smooth-purity and the master source path.
